A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 20 pages of each version, including Appendix A proofs and Appendix B results and experimental details, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning and calibration experiments, kernel memory and timing benchmarks, and supplementary analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Table 1 calibration evaluations and Tables 2–3 kernel benchmarks.

M1.justification: The label-smoothing objective, memory-efficient forward pass in Algorithm 1, backward computation, and kernel components remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, Tulu3Mixture, and OpenHermes for fine-tuning and retain MMLU, HellaSwag, and ARC-Easy evaluations. Appendix B adds or removes no coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains SFT without smoothing, while Tables 2–3 retain the same PyTorch baseline, torch.compile, Cut-Cross Entropy, Liger Kernels, and torchtune comparisons in their respective settings.

E3.justification: Both retain five-shot evaluation, the same metrics and model configurations, AdamW, batch size 128, dropout 0.1, and identical learning-rate and smoothing sweeps. Kernel benchmark conditions also match.

E4.justification: The model-size and smoothing analyses, appendix reliability diagrams, training-curve comparisons, and Table 3 ablations of vocabulary sorting, gradient filtering, and fused computation are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports seed/run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–10 retain identical results. For example, Tulu3Mixture LLaMA3-8B with smoothing 0.1 retains MMLU ECE 0.012, and the smoothed kernel retains combined memory/time of 1,164 MB and 72.9 ms.

T1.justification: Mathematical statements, assumptions, equations, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Relabeling Propositions 3.3–3.4 and Lemma 4.1 as 'Theorem' in appendix headings and references does not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about SFT miscalibration, label smoothing's benefits and limitations, and efficient smoothed cross-entropy computation.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations involving feature diversity, vocabulary and hidden-size constraints, temperature scaling, and softcapping. The stated calibration and computational limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures and reproducibility information match, including the H100-SXM5 hardware, PyTorch/CUDA versions, open-instruct commit e363290, hyperparameter sweeps, repository references, and evaluation prompt in Appendix B.

R1.justification: No cited works are added or removed. Related-work discussion, attribution of theoretical arguments, and positioning against existing calibration methods and efficient kernels remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 swaps the first two authors, adds Jerry Huang as a corresponding author, changes several 'Appendix' references to 'Section,' and changes some appendix labels to 'Theorem.' These labels now differ from the retained main-text Proposition/Lemma labels; the narrative and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author footnote causes limited reflow across pages 1–2, with small spacing and wrapping changes elsewhere. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–3 retain their content, structure, and placement; Table 2's caption changes 'Appendix B' to 'Section B.'

improvement.justification: The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, conclusions, and reproducibility information are unchanged. Author/contact edits and minor reflow provide no substantive quality improvement. The new appendix theorem-label inconsistencies slightly reduce editorial precision, but matching numbers and unchanged statements keep the proofs identifiable.
